analysis.file_name: Morgan Stanley - What Does the Power Shortfall Mean for Semis - Oct 5 2026.pdf
analysis.title: What Does the Power Shortfall Mean for Semis?
key_insights: Morgan Stanley sizes the US data center power shortfall at 57 GW over 2026-28. Net of 'time to power' solutions it is 32 GW, or 34% of demanded power. The total is unchanged in this update.
Nvidia management commentary confirms there is not enough power to meet demand. MS says more chips are being built than there are places to put them.

MS expects no impact on Nvidia and Broadcom 2027 numbers. It cites conservative guidance that allows for a land, power and shell (LPS) shortage, management visibility into chip placement, geographic expansion, and Nvidia's higher tokens per GW.
Nvidia and Broadcom have given 12 month outlooks totaling about $800bn of AI revenue. MS does not see this at risk today but says power makes upside harder.

Broadcom may already show the effect. It guided FY27 AI revenue well above $100bn in March and to $115bn in September, less upside than investors expected. MS says this puts some pressure on AMD, although warrant arrangements with AMD's largest customers de-risk its estimates.
MS sees a risk that ASICs lose share to GPUs in a power-constrained market because ASICs produce fewer tokens per watt. The biggest ASIC users face the highest risk of inadequate LPS access.

In a bear case the disruption would be largest at the tail of the supply chain: memory, optics, and small-dollar parts such as power management and analog chips. These are the likeliest to be over-ordered and are where shortage-driven pricing supports revenue and EPS.

If deployable capacity falls short of chip supply, customers could push out deliveries or cancel orders. MS thinks GPU inventory holding is limited because newer chips arrive annually and vendors can reroute orders to ready customers.
Nvidia is the preferred way to express the power risk. About half of its business is outside traditional hyperscalers, and 55 of its 80 listed cloud partners are outside the US.

Power access is concentrating among large, credit-worthy players. Hyperscalers are energizing faster, while smaller neoclouds without credit backing, non-US players and ASIC-based deployments are at risk. MS is more bullish on hyperscalers as a result.

MS Internet forecasts hyperscaler and neocloud capacity additions of 22 GW in 2026, 32 GW in 2027 and 39 GW in 2028, equal to 94%, 64% and 57% of global capacity additions. MS says this could squeeze out other players.
MS hears Amazon is well positioned to secure power. Google adds the most incremental capacity in 2027 and 2028 and so could face more difficulty securing power for the compute it is buying.

International expansion cannot absorb the US shortfall. MS cuts its US share of global compute to 55% from 60%. Europe has limited spillover room because of power constraints and slow planning permission, and the Middle East is hampered by geopolitical instability.

Behind-the-meter (BTM) generation is the main upside driver. MS models 11-49 GW of BTM turbines and engines, with 19 GW in the base case. The 11 GW low end is firm contracted deals and the 49 GW high end is factory capacity.

MS Utilities tracks 25-30 GW of manufacturer orders for 2026-28 and expects developers to approach 15 GW or more of annual BTM additions from 2028. If 30 GW of BTM comes online by 2028, the net shortfall falls to 21 GW.
Bloom Energy fuel cells are a key beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall. MS forecasts 6 GW for 2026-28 and sees possible upside from reported site expansion.

Labor and politics limit the BTM upside. CSIS estimates 140K+ extra skilled tradespeople are needed by 2030. The current labor base supports 10-20 GW a year of gas additions, and moratoriums and public pushback on data centers add friction.

The shortfall worsens after 2027. The year-by-year net shortfall is 9 GW in 2026, 5 GW in 2027, 18 GW in 2028 and 35 GW in 2029, which raises the premium for securing power in the US and capacity abroad.
MS values AVGO at 28x CY2027e ModelWare EPS of $18.04 (about 26x non-GAAP EPS of $19.63) and NVDA at about 20x its CY27 EPS estimate of $15.01.

market_movers.rationale: MS prefers Nvidia as the way to handle power risk because of its broadest geographic and customer footprint and higher tokens per watt. It says Nvidia has line of sight into chip placement and can make 2027 numbers.
MS is convinced Broadcom can meet its 12 month outlook. It flags that the September FY27 AI revenue guide of $115bn offered less upside than expected and that ASIC share loss to GPUs is a risk.
MS says the power constraint puts some pressure on AMD, but warrant dynamics with its largest customers significantly de-risk its estimates.
MS calls Bloom Energy a key beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall and sees possible upside to its 6 GW fuel cell forecast for 2026-28.

sector_views.rationale: Large, credit-worthy players with revenue visibility are getting power access faster, and MS says it is more bullish on hyperscalers.

sector_views.sector: Memory, optics, power management and analog semis
sector_views.rationale: No rating change is given. MS flags these as the most exposed components in a bear case because they are likeliest to be over-ordered and are supported by shortage-driven pricing.
No rating change is given. MS sees a risk that ASICs lose share to GPUs in a power-constrained environment because of lower token production per watt.

earnings_insights: Broadcom guided FY27 AI revenue well above $100bn in March (company guidance, a forecast) and to $115bn in its most recent guidance from September, which MS says is much less upside than investors anticipated.
Nvidia and Broadcom together have given 12 month AI revenue outlooks of about $800bn (company guidance, a forecast). MS does not see this at risk from power today.
MS estimates, not reported figures: AVGO CY2027e ModelWare EPS of $18.04 (about 26x non-GAAP EPS of $19.63) and NVDA CY27 EPS of $15.01.

Broadcom CEO Hock Tan on Sept 8, 2026 said the outlook is a judged number based on memory wafer supply and the readiness of power sites. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Aug 26 and Sept 10, 2026 said Nvidia has greater visibility upstream and downstream and tracks every gigawatt of land, power and shell.
crypto_views: Grid access owned by former Bitcoin mining companies is one 'time to power' source. MS counts crypto sites as 2 GW in 2026, 6 GW by 2027, 12 GW by 2028 and 18 GW by 2029 on a cumulative basis, counted within DCs under construction or turbines.
MS expects higher urgency and premia for repurposing former Bitcoin mining sites' grid access, and points to a separate report on ways to play this.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Nvidia over ASIC-exposed names given higher tokens per watt in a power-constrained market
trade_ideas.rationale: The power risk drives MS's preference for Nvidia, which has the broadest geographic and customer footprint and the greater tokens per watt.
trade_ideas.risk: AI end markets don't materialize as expected, or AMD reemerges as a viable GPU competitor.

trade_ideas.description: Bloom Energy as a beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall
trade_ideas.rationale: Bloom Energy is a key beneficiary of the shortfall, and MS sees potential upside to its 6 GW fuel cell forecast.

risk_factors: Land, power and shell shortage worsening beyond 2027 as people, power and politics constraints build.
ASIC share loss to GPUs because of lower token production per watt.
Order pushouts or cancellations in memory, optics, power management and analog parts if chips cannot be deployed.
Smaller, less credit-worthy neoclouds and non-US players being squeezed out of power access.
Skilled labor shortage, with CSIS estimating 140K+ more tradespeople needed by 2030.
Political pushback and moratoriums on data centers.
Geopolitical instability limiting Middle East expansion.
Broadcom downside risks: losing networking share to Nvidia, uncompetitive ASICs, VMware execution.
Nvidia downside risks: AI end markets underdelivering, AMD emerging as a viable GPU competitor, cloud customers outside Google developing competitive custom hardware.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 table: incremental global data center demand of 32, 56, 86 and 124 GW for 2026-2029, less a US power shortfall of 9, 5, 18 and 35 GW, giving global energized capacity of 23, 51, 68 and 89 GW. Hyperscaler and neocloud share of capacity additions is 94%, 64% and 57%.
Exhibit 3 waterfall: 97 GW total US data center power demand less 21 GW under construction and 19 GW utility grid access gives a 57 GW shortfall, reduced by time-to-power solutions to a net 32 GW.

Exhibit 4 table: low, midpoint and high net shortfalls of 42, 32 and 0 GW, equal to 43%, 34% and 0% of 2026-28 US data center deployments. The probability-weighted time-to-power solutions total 15, 24 and 57 GW, and MS says the midpoint outcome is most likely.
Exhibit 5 tables: cumulative midpoint net shortfall of 9, 15, 32 and 68 GW for 2026-2029, and annual midpoint shortfall of 9, 5, 18 and 35 GW.
geopolitical: An AWS data center was hit by Iran strikes, which MS cites as a reason expansion into the Middle East is difficult given geopolitical instability.
Growing political pushback against data centers and AI, including moratoriums and public perception, is slowing US build-outs.
Data center growth outside the US (Korea, Singapore, India, Australia, China, Europe) is increasing, but Europe is limited by power constraints and slow planning permission.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia and Broadcom management have line of sight into chip placement, guidance already allows for an LPS shortage, and Nvidia's higher tokens per GW and global footprint help in a constrained market. MS does not see 2027 forecasts at risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Beyond 2027 the shortfall worsens, ASICs may lose share to GPUs, and memory, optics, power management and analog parts could see order pushouts or cancellations. Broadcom's September guide of $115bn showed less upside than expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If there's chip capacity expected to come online that cannot be deployed at data centers, we could see customers push out delivery or start canceling orders.

tension_points.bull_case: BTM turbines of 11-49 GW and Bloom fuel cells above the 6 GW forecast could narrow the shortfall. Manufacturer orders of 25-30 GW are tracked and developers could add 15 GW or more per year from 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Labor availability, complex engineering work, permitting and political pushback limit how fast BTM capacity can come online. The existing labor base supports 10-20 GW of annual gas additions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If 30 GW of BTM power successfully comes online from 2026-28, the net US shortfall would fall to 21 GW from 32 GW.

theme_stances.key_argument: The power shortfall is real and affecting semis, but Nvidia and Broadcom can make 2027 numbers, with risk concentrated in ASICs, memory, optics and other components.
theme_stances.evidence: The power shortfall is real and affecting semis

theme_stances.theme: asic share loss under power constraint
theme_stances.key_argument: ASICs produce fewer tokens per watt, so they risk losing share to GPUs when power is the binding constraint.
theme_stances.evidence: ASICs will lose share in a power-constrained environment relative to GPUs

theme_stances.key_argument: Providers with a viable path to supplying data center power in 2027 and 2028 should be able to enter lucrative agreements.
theme_stances.evidence: Bloom Energy is a key beneficiary of this
